report:
Theorems A–C, ordinary-open localization, and the stated finite quadratic towers are established under their stated hypotheses. This is a PASS for the partial theorem; original P06.2 recognition remains open.

I reconstructed the supporting proofs in §§3–9 without importing earlier verdicts or artifact claims. The finite-tensor argument retains nonreduced algebras. The fibre calculation gives precisely one fixed point or two interchanged points, and the compact-complement argument legitimately shrinks around the whole fibre. Compact inverse images and the minimal-prime argument establish the support and purity properties actually needed. Restriction of the finite ground field preserves the carrier, analytic-unit germs, moment descriptions, and ordinary-form nullity criteria.

For A, the three trace rows have unit determinants. Consequently two traces cannot simultaneously have smaller magnitude than the maximum, including in characteristic two. This proves (4) throughout the retained neighbourhood, including cancellation loci. Polarization gives every scalar pair δᵢδⱼ. The tripod identity is zero on each ray and on every compact moment image, so it is an identity in the ordinary sheaf. Both zero cases in §5.2 are covered by strict inequalities on full neighbourhoods. Adding the tripod identity to its conjugate gives exactly (10); combining its alternating part with dQᵢⱼ gives δᵢdδⱼ. Differentiating then supplies all three differential-pair types in (13), since unit-logarithmic coordinates have zero d'd'' as ordinary forms. Pairing anti-invariant symbols proves descent in every bidegree. All constructions use one finite unit list and one shrink, independent of polynomial degree. Divisions by two occur only in real coefficients.

For B, the Euclidean extension respects the required closed-subset hypothesis. Symmetrization includes differential factors, and Gaussian convolution followed by polynomial approximation supplies coefficient convergence through order two. The two-point case uses analytic gluing on disjoint opens, with invariant units descending algebraically. The finite ordinary partition gives a fixed compact D; extension by zero is valid because each cutoff support lies compactly inside its open. Enlarging the upstairs moments to include cutoff descriptions leaves a finite collection independent of the approximation index. The product rule therefore controls the differentiated errors in those fixed charts.

The measure estimate is valid in arbitrary pure dimension: the determinant-minor calculation bounds every coefficient contraction by binomial(r,n) times the positive diagonal contraction. The factor n! in ζ is correct. Lower-dimensional cells contribute no top measure, and actual positive calibration weights multiply both sides of the inequality. Compact charts give finite dominating measures. Hence differentiated total variation tends to zero on π⁻¹(D), where the continuous finite multiplier is bounded. This supplies the needed pairing convergence directly, without assuming convergence in the full smooth-test topology.

For C, the two normalizations are correctly distinguished. I checked the relevant statements and proof bodies in [CLD v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2): scalar calibration compatibility uses actual Artinian fibre-algebra degrees and their decomposition after extension; the calibration construction retains determinant indices. Scalar projection introduces no extension-degree factor. Finite ground-field restriction introduces factor two, which cancels when the semilinear involution is treated as a K-analytic isomorphism. Averaging consequently preserves the upstairs pairing. Equation (22), followed by the fixed-support approximation, proves ascent; (22) alone proves descent. The boundary inclusion in [GR v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13548v2) has the required field quantifier. The ambient properties persist on ordinary opens and at every tower stage.

The Q₂ example satisfies (H). No normalization, conductor, curve-recognition, regularization, or unrestricted Galois-descent theorem is imported into this proof. Those additional recognition obligations therefore do not obstruct this partial theorem. Compilation and finite diagnostics provide no theorem verification and were not used as evidence.

Harmless wording clarification: ‘finitely many cells’ in §2(5) refers to each compact moment chart. No substantive repair is required.

passages.statement: For a complete non-Archimedean field k and a k-affinoid algebra A, M(A) is compact Hausdorff, A is noetherian with closed ideals, and the kernel map M(A)→Spec A is surjective. The spectrum of a nonzero affinoid algebra is nonempty. CLD v2, §§11.1.1–2.

For a complete non-Archimedean field k and a k-affinoid algebra A, M(A) is compact Hausdorff, A is noetherian with closed ideals, and the kernel map M(A)→Spec A is surjective. The spectrum of a nonzero affinoid algebra is nonempty. CLD v2, §§11.1.1–2.

For a complete non-Archimedean field k and a k-affinoid algebra A, M(A) is compact Hausdorff, A is noetherian with closed ideals, and the kernel map M(A)→Spec A is surjective. The spectrum of a nonzero affinoid algebra is nonempty. CLD v2, §§11.1.1–2.

Every ordinary open of a k-analytic space is an analytic domain. Affinoid neighbourhoods form a neighbourhood basis in a good k-analytic space. In an affinoid space, every prescribed ordinary open neighbourhood of a point contains a rational affinoid neighbourhood of that point. The analytic structural sheaf satisfies O(M(A))=A. CLD v2, §§11.1.5–8.

Affinoid fibre products are computed by completed tensor products: M(B)×M(A)M(C)=M(B⊗̂_A C). For every complete extension L/k, scalar extension of M(A) is M(A⊗̂_k L), and the scalar projection X_L→X is surjective. CLD v2, §11.1.9.
If A is a k-affinoid algebra and B is a finite A-algebra equipped with its finite-module Banach topology, then B is k-affinoid. CLD v2, §11.4.4.

For strict affinoid spaces, analytic dimension equals Krull dimension. Scalar extension preserves analytic dimension. If X=M(A) and X_i=M(A/P_i) for the minimal primes P_i of A, then dim_x X=sup_{x∈X_i} dim X_i. Analytic domains preserve local analytic dimension. Analytic separatedness implies topological separatedness. CLD v2, §§11.2.2–3.

For every morphism X→Y of k-analytic spaces and every analytic extension field L/k, the relative analytic boundaries satisfy ∂(X_L/Y_L)⊆π⁻¹(∂(X/Y)). In particular, boundarylessness is preserved by scalar extension. GR v2, §2.11(5′).

Every ordinary smooth real CLD (p,q)-form on a topologically separated analytic space admits an ordinary open cover with moment pullback representations by smooth coefficient forms on paralinéaire subsets containing the moment images. A smooth coefficient form on a paralinéaire subset P of a finite-dimensional affine space extends to an ambient open U whenever P is closed in U; such an ambient open can be chosen for these representations. CLD v2, Proposition 15.1.1(b), §3.3.3, and Lemma 1.9.4.

Every ordinary smooth real CLD (p,q)-form on a topologically separated analytic space admits an ordinary open cover with moment pullback representations by smooth coefficient forms on paralinéaire subsets containing the moment images. A smooth coefficient form on a paralinéaire subset P of a finite-dimensional affine space extends to an ambient open U whenever P is closed in U; such an ambient open can be chosen for these representations. CLD v2, Proposition 15.1.1(b), §3.3.3, and Lemma 1.9.4.

For a G-tropical chart f:X→E and a coefficient form α on a paralinéaire subset containing f(X), its pullback is zero in the G-form sheaf exactly when α restricts to zero on f(V) for every compact domain V⊆X. For compact X the corresponding criterion holds in the compact presheaf. Degree-zero G-forms inject into numerical functions. CLD v2, Propositions 3.4.1 and 3.4.4 and §3.4.6.

Ordinary smooth real CLD forms form a sheaf for the ordinary topology and are stable under d′, d′′, J, and exterior product. Pullback in the G-form sheaves is functorial and commutes with these differential operations and exterior product. CLD v2, §§6.2.1–2 and 3.3.10–12.

Ordinary smooth real CLD forms form a sheaf for the ordinary topology and are stable under d′, d′′, J, and exterior product. Pullback in the G-form sheaves is functorial and commutes with these differential operations and exterior product. CLD v2, §§6.2.1–2 and 3.3.10–12.

A good topologically separated analytic space is locally holomorphically separated. On a locally holomorphically separated analytic space X, for a closed subset F countable at infinity and an ordinary open cover (U_i) of F, there are locally finite nonnegative ordinary smooth functions θ_i with compact support in U_i and sum one near F. CLD v2, §15.2.2 and Corollary 15.2.9.

A topologically separated analytic space pure of dimension n, equipped with its analytic boundary and canonical calibration, is a tropical space of level n. For an analytic domain V, its induced tropical structure agrees with the structure arising from its own analytic structure. CLD v2, Theorem 15.7.1 and §15.7.2.

The canonical calibration on skeletal subsets of a topologically separated analytic space of level n is standard and compatible with restriction to analytic domains. On a convenient top-dimensional moment cell it is constructed from a finite positive constant finite-flat degree and the pulled-back standard volume vector. CLD v2, §§14.3.1–5 and Proposition 14.2.2.

Smooth top forms on a calibrated tropical space have locally finite calibrated Radon measures. A locally integrable real numerical function u defines the order-zero integration current [u] by [u](ω)=∫uω_Rad for compact ordinary top forms ω. Continuous finite numerical functions are locally integrable. CLD v2, §§5.7.2 and 5.8.3–6, Corollary 7.2.10, and §7.3.5.

Compact moment images are finite polyhedra, and every compact G-tropical chart on a space of level n is pleasant with tropical polyhedron the top-dimensional part of its image. For a pleasant chart f and a Borel coefficient (n,n)-form α, local integrability is equivalent to calibrated local integrability on its tropical polyhedron; when locally integrable, f_trop,*((f*α)_Rad)=⟨α,μ_Πf⟩_Rad, with the corresponding integration equality. CLD v2, Theorem 12.2.4, §5.4.4, and Proposition 5.10.1(c,d).

For a topologically separated analytic space X of level n, a skeletal subset Σ with canonical calibration μ, and a complete extension L/k, the extended skeletal subset Σ_L has canonical calibration μ_L satisfying π_*μ_L=μ. For a morphism f:Y→X, a complete extension L/k, an isolated zero-dimensional fibre point y over x, and a lift x_L of x, deg_y(f)=Σ_z deg_z(f_L), where z ranges over the lifts of y mapping to x_L. These degrees are dimensions of the actual local finite fibre algebras, including their Artinian multiplicities. CLD v2, Proposition 14.3.6 and §§13.3.1–3.

For a topologically separated analytic space X of level n, a skeletal subset Σ with canonical calibration μ, and a complete extension L/k, the extended skeletal subset Σ_L has canonical calibration μ_L satisfying π_*μ_L=μ. For a morphism f:Y→X, a complete extension L/k, an isolated zero-dimensional fibre point y over x, and a lift x_L of x, deg_y(f)=Σ_z deg_z(f_L), where z ranges over the lifts of y mapping to x_L. These degrees are dimensions of the actual local finite fibre algebras, including their Artinian multiplicities. CLD v2, Proposition 14.3.6 and §§13.3.1–3.

For a k-analytic space X of level n, a complete extension L/k, and an (n,n) G-form ω with tropically Borel coefficients, scalar projection satisfies π_*(ω_L,Bor)=ω_Bor. If ω is locally integrable, π_*(ω_L,Rad)=ω_Rad. There is no extension-degree factor. CLD v2, Proposition 15.3.1.

For a finite extension F/k and an F-analytic space Z of level n, its same-carrier restricted k-analytic structure Z_0 has the same dimension and skeletal subsets. Their canonical calibrations satisfy μ_Z0=[F:k]μ_Z. CLD v2, Remark 14.4.3.

Let f:Y→X be a morphism between k-analytic spaces of level n that is finite over the complement of a Zariski closed subset of X of dimension less than n. For p∈{n−1,n} and a locally integrable (p,n) G-form ω, f*ω is locally integrable and f_*((f*ω)_Rad)=dc(f)ω_Rad. In particular, a degree-one analytic isomorphism preserves the calibrated pairing under change of variables. CLD v2, §15.4.1 and Proposition 15.4.3.

On a tropical space, the CLD differential operators on currents are defined by signed transposition of the operators on compact ordinary smooth forms and satisfy ⟨d′d′′S,α⟩=⟨S,d′d′′α⟩ for every current S and every compact ordinary smooth test α of the complementary bidegree. CLD v2, §§7.7.1–3 and Lemma 7.7.5.
